items.title: Superstocks.ai
items.summary: Making messy information easier to work with.
items.problem: Public-markets research brings together structured data, screening and longer analysis. I’m interested in how AI can help turn that material into something I can query and work through.
approach: I’ve worked on guarded SQL agents and screening workflows around research data.
I’ve connected multi-agent analysis workflows with ClickHouse analytics.
I’ve also worked with retrieval pipelines using Pinecone to bring research context into the workflow.
items.outcome: I work across research tools, retrieval and structured queries, bringing the source material and the analysis into the same workflow.
items.reflection: I keep the source material, the query and the generated interpretation distinct. A well-written answer is easier to assess when I can see what it was based on.

items.title: Experimental Brain
items.summary: Connecting what a model observes with what a small actor does next.
items.problem: I wanted a way to inspect the gap between an observation, an action and a language model’s description of what might happen next.
approach: I connected a V-JEPA 2 encoder to short video samples and recorded the resulting embeddings with their model revision and preprocessing details.
I built a small grid simulation with an explicit rule-based policy. Motion allows a step; a path planner chooses a route around an obstacle.
I kept the optional LLM narration separate from perception and control. I can step through the actor and export a trace of the run.
items.outcome: The site includes real recorded V-JEPA outputs and a separate live-perception service. The browser can replay recordings without downloading the encoder. Live perception requires a configured service; the actor is a demonstration, not a trained robotics policy.
items.reflection: A similarity score is not a confidence estimate, and a plausible narration is not an observation. I make those distinctions visible in the experiment.

items.title: Qwen fine-tuning
items.summary: Looking at what changes when I fine-tune a model—and how I check it.
items.problem: I’ve been working with Qwen fine-tuning to explore how a model learns from source material. The question extends beyond training loss: I want to know whether its answers are supported and whether it retains other capabilities.
approach: I’ve worked with LoRA adapters rather than updating every model weight.
I’ve kept source-specific training examples separate from general examples, with answer-token losses and isolated sequence packing.
I’ve used held-out questions and source-based answer reviews alongside training logs. I’ve also explored regularization against the base model’s responses.
items.outcome: I’m comparing training choices with answer reviews on held-out questions. This is an experiment in training and evaluation. The browser playground on this site uses a separate, unmodified pretrained Qwen model.
items.reflection: A lower loss and a better answer are different checks. Source-word overlap can help me inspect an answer, but it cannot establish that the answer addresses the question.

items.title: Robot fleet scaling
items.summary: Supporting more concurrent robots on the same hardware.
items.problem: The fleet platform needed to handle more concurrent robots without a corresponding hardware increase.
approach: I worked on backend performance and platform scaling for robot fleets.
I focused on bottlenecks and resource use while supporting concurrent robot workloads.
items.outcome: The platform scaled from approximately 8–10 to 100 concurrent robots on the same hardware.

items.title: Frontend performance & scale
items.summary: Faster frontends, better observability and billing dashboards at Razorpay.
items.problem: At Razorpay I worked on billing and CRM product surfaces that needed to load quickly, stay available and be cheap to serve.
approach: I built dashboards for digital billing and CRM, covering customer engagement insights, campaign creation and multi-tenant bill management, with Node.js, Express and Kubernetes.
I worked on infrastructure upgrades, including a React 18 migration that cut the bundle size by 90% and CloudFront costs by 50%, and a move from Create React App to Rspack.
I set up real-time alerts and observability with Coralogix, Grafana and Coralogix RUM, and worked on a microfrontend architecture to migrate a legacy site to Razorpay PG.
items.outcome: The bundle shrank by 90% and CloudFront costs dropped by 50%. I also helped raise application availability to 99.92%.

items.title: Research retrieval pipelines
items.summary: Bringing source context into research workflows.
items.problem: I’ve worked on connecting language models to research material using retrieval. That includes the movement of data through indexing, search and downstream analysis.
approach: I’ve used Pinecone for vector retrieval in RAG workflows.
I’ve connected retrieved context to analysis pipelines.
I’ve worked across the backend, deployment and monitoring parts of those workflows.
items.outcome: This work connects vector search with the backend and analysis workflows that consume the retrieved material.

items.title: Prompt Studio
items.summary: A writing assistant with streamed responses and conversation controls.
items.problem: I wanted a chat interface that could handle technical writing, including code, tables and longer responses.
approach: I built around Next.js, TypeScript, shadcn/ui and the AI SDK.
The public repository documents streamed Markdown, conversation history and responsive navigation.
The interface includes stop, regenerate and copy controls.
items.outcome: The source is available on GitHub. I haven’t published usage or adoption figures.

items.title: Freight platform frontend
items.summary: Scaling a logistics frontend to new regions, with real-time and accounting features.
items.problem: At WIZ, a freight and logistics platform, the frontend needed to work across multiple regions and support accounting and collaboration workflows.
approach: I revamped and refactored the frontend codebase so it could scale to multiple regions.
I built real-time task sharing over WebSockets and the UI for searching vessel schedules.
I used Next.js to build accounting features, including invoices, bulk payments and a Zoho Books integration, and set up a Docker Compose development environment for the microservices.
items.outcome: The Docker Compose environment saved the team about two months a year and kept the git history clean. I was promoted from SDE 1 to SDE 2.

items.title: Apparel try-on web app
items.summary: Letting shoppers see outfits on a model that resembles them.
items.problem: Mad Street Den needed a web app where customers could try different combinations of apparel and see the result on a model that resembles them.
approach: I built the responsive web app on my own in React and Bootstrap.
I cut subsequent dev build times by 87.5% using webpack dev server and hot module reloading.
As an intern, I rewrote about 40% of the codebase to functional components and hooks.
items.outcome: I was promoted within six months for exceeding goals and supporting the company culture.
